hot.title: Continuous Latent Diffusion Language Model
hot.summary: Cola DLM is a hierarchical latent-space diffusion language model that frames text generation by separating global semantic organization in a continuous latent space from local textual realization. It exhibits strong scaling performance on reasoning-intensive tasks and offers a robust framework for unified multimodal generative modeling.

hot.title: AI Co-Mathematician: Accelerating Mathematicians with Agentic AI
hot.summary: Google DeepMind's AI Co-Mathematician offers a stateful, agent-based workbench designed to support the full workflow of mathematical research, integrating AI tools into a human-centric collaborative environment. The system achieved a new high score on the FrontierMath Tier 4 benchmark, solving 23 out of 48 problems, and assisted professional mathematicians in resolving open problems and gaining new insights.

hot.title: SkillOS: Learning Skill Curation for Self-Evolving Agents
hot.summary: SkillOS, developed by researchers from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and Google Cloud AI Research, introduces an experience-driven reinforcement learning framework that enables Large Language Model (LLM) agents to automatically curate reusable skills. This framework facilitates continuous self-evolution, leading to improved task success rates and increased efficiency across diverse agentic and reasoning benchmarks.

hot.title: Reconstruction or Semantics? What Makes a Latent Space Useful for Robotic World Models
hot.summary: A study on action-conditioned Latent Diffusion Models (LDMs) for robotics reveals that semantic-aligned latent spaces consistently outperform reconstruction-aligned spaces in policy evaluation, action planning, and task success preservation for complex manipulation tasks. Semantic latents demonstrated a 9.8 percentage point increase in VLA success rates and 13.6 percentage point improvement in out-of-distribution robustness.

hot.title: Manifold Steering Reveals the Shared Geometry of Neural Network Representation and Behavior
hot.summary: Researchers at Stanford University and collaborators revealed that the intrinsic geometry of neural network representations is tightly coupled with model behavior, proposing "manifold steering" as a geometry-aware intervention that yields more natural and coherent behavioral changes than conventional linear steering. This approach demonstrated a 2.8x average improvement in naturalness across language and vision tasks and generalized to multi-dimensional concept control.

hot.title: Lecture Notes on Statistical Physics and Neural Networks
hot.summary: Lecture notes from Humboldt University Berlin connect classical statistical physics concepts, such as the Boltzmann-Gibbs distribution, phase transitions, and the renormalization group, to the theoretical foundations of neural networks and deep learning. The work explicates parallels between models like Hopfield networks and Boltzmann machines and modern AI architectures, suggesting statistical physics offers a framework for understanding empirical phenomena like scaling laws in large language models.

hot.title: Skill1: Unified Evolution of Skill-Augmented Agents via Reinforcement Learning
hot.summary: Researchers developed Skill1, a unified reinforcement learning framework that simultaneously optimizes skill selection, utilization, and distillation in LLM agents using a single task-outcome signal. This approach achieved superior success rates on complex interactive environments like ALFWorld and WebShop while fostering a more diverse and effective skill library.

hot.title: On-Policy Distillation
hot.summary: This work introduces on-policy distillation, a post-training method for large language models that combines the on-policy relevance of reinforcement learning with dense, token-level feedback from a teacher model. The approach achieved 70% on the AIME'24 mathematical reasoning benchmark with Qwen3-8B and demonstrated a 30x cost reduction compared to off-policy distillation, while also recovering instruction-following abilities in personalized models.

hot.title: ReActor: Reinforcement Learning for Physics-Aware Motion Retargeting
hot.summary: ReActor, a framework from Disney Research, uses a bilevel optimization scheme to adapt human kinematic motion to diverse robotic morphologies by integrating reinforcement learning with physics simulation. This approach generates physically plausible motions with zero ground or self-penetration, which significantly improves downstream reinforcement learning success rates by up to 15.22 percentage points on various humanoid and quadruped robots.

hot.title: ZAYA1-8B Technical Report
hot.summary: ZAYA1-8B, an 8B total parameter Mixture-of-Experts model with 700M active parameters, demonstrates competitive reasoning performance on mathematics and coding benchmarks. This model's capabilities are further enhanced by a novel Markovian RSA test-time compute method, narrowing the performance gap to frontier models while maintaining a constrained active parameter count.

hot.title: Can RL Teach Long-Horizon Reasoning to LLMs? Expressiveness Is Key
hot.summary: Researchers developed SCALELOGIC, a synthetic environment for studying large language model (LLM) reasoning, finding that reinforcement learning (RL) training compute scales as a power-law with reasoning depth, and this scaling exponent increases with logical expressiveness, directly impacting transfer to real-world benchmarks.

hot.title: Recursive Multi-Agent Systems
hot.summary: RecursiveMAS introduces a framework that integrates recursive computation into multi-agent systems, enabling agents to refine collaborative reasoning through iterative latent-space interactions rather than explicit text. This approach leads to average accuracy improvements of up to 20.2% and inference speedups of up to 2.4x compared to text-based recursive multi-agent systems, significantly reducing token usage.

hot.title: RLDX-1 Technical Report
hot.summary: RLDX-1, developed by RLWRLD and KAIST, is a unified Vision-Language-Action (VLA) system for dexterous robotic manipulation that integrates motion awareness, long-term memory, and physical sensing. It demonstrates superior performance over existing frontier VLA models across diverse simulation benchmarks and real-world tasks, including complex humanoid operations and contact-rich scenarios, with a notable 97.8% success rate on LIBERO and significant improvements in functional capabilities.

hot.title: D-OPSD: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Continuously Tuning Step-Distilled Diffusion Models
hot.summary: Researchers developed D-OPSD, an on-policy self-distillation framework, to enable continuous fine-tuning of efficient few-step diffusion models without sacrificing their original inference speed or image quality. This method notably outperformed standard fine-tuning and reinforcement learning approaches in learning new concepts and generalizing them while preserving core capabilities.

hot.title: When to Trust Imagination: Adaptive Action Execution for World Action Models
hot.summary: A new framework, FFDC-WAM, enables World Action Models to adaptively execute actions by continuously verifying their predicted future observations against real-world sensory input. This approach improves robotic task success rates on challenging manipulation tasks while reducing computational overhead for simpler, predictable actions, mimicking human-like adaptive planning.

hot.title: MolmoAct2: Action Reasoning Models for Real-world Deployment
hot.summary: MolmoAct2, developed by the Allen Institute for AI and the University of Washington, is a fully open-source action reasoning model designed for real-world robot deployment, enhancing generalizability and efficiency. It incorporates an embodied reasoning VLM backbone and a continuous action expert, achieving up to 87.1% success on real-world DROID tasks with unseen objects and a 2.42x speedup in control rate compared to unoptimized inference.

hot.title: A Case-Driven Multi-Agent Framework for E-Commerce Search Relevance
hot.summary: Researchers at ByteDance developed a case-driven multi-agent framework to automate the entire e-commerce search relevance optimization pipeline, replacing human-centric workflows for identifying, diagnosing, and resolving suboptimal search results. This system achieved a cumulative online win-rate gain of 4.36% on the main market and reduced labeling costs by 75.4%.

hot.title: ProgramBench: Can Language Models Rebuild Programs From Scratch?
hot.summary: ProgramBench introduces a new benchmark to evaluate large language models' capacity for holistic software development from scratch, providing only a compiled executable and its documentation. The evaluation revealed that current leading models achieve a 0.0% full resolution rate, struggling with high-level architectural design and system decomposition.

hot.title: OpenSearch-VL: An Open Recipe for Frontier Multimodal Search Agents
hot.summary: OpenSearch-VL introduces an open-source recipe for training multimodal deep search agents, providing high-quality, openly available training data, a diverse tool environment, and an improved reinforcement learning algorithm. It demonstrates substantial performance improvements across multiple multimodal knowledge-intensive QA and web-search benchmarks, achieving an average score of 61.6 with its 30B-A3B model, a 13.8-point gain over a strong baseline.

hot.title: Recursive Agent Optimization
hot.summary: Recursive Agent Optimization (RAO) trains large language models to intrinsically leverage recursive delegation, allowing them to overcome context window limitations and generalize to harder tasks. This approach achieved up to 95% success on context-constrained tasks and demonstrated faster learning and improved generalization compared to non-recursive baselines.

likes.title: Perception Encoder: The best visual embeddings are not at the output of  the network
likes.summary: Perception Encoder introduces a family of vision models that achieve state-of-the-art performance across diverse vision and vision-language tasks, demonstrating that general, high-quality visual features can be extracted from the intermediate layers of a single, contrastively-trained network. It provides specific alignment tuning methods to make these features accessible for tasks ranging from zero-shot classification to dense spatial prediction and multimodal language understanding.

likes.title: TTRL: Test-Time Reinforcement Learning
likes.summary: TTRL is a framework enabling Large Language Models to self-improve through Reinforcement Learning on unlabeled test data, using self-generated rewards derived from majority voting. This approach substantially boosts performance on complex reasoning tasks, with one model achieving a 211% improvement on AIME 2024, by fostering a self-reinforcing learning loop.

likes.title: Inference-Time Scaling for Generalist Reward Modeling
likes.summary: DeepSeek-AI and Tsinghua University developed Self-Principled Critique Tuning (SPCT) and DeepSeek-GRM models, a pointwise generative reward modeling approach that achieves state-of-the-art performance in generalist reward benchmarks. This method demonstrates effective inference-time scalability, allowing smaller models to match or exceed the performance of much larger models by leveraging increased compute during inference, thereby improving LLM alignment.

likes.title: Does Reinforcement Learning Really Incentivize Reasoning Capacity in LLMs Beyond the Base Model?
likes.summary: Research from Tsinghua University reveals that current Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) primarily enhances the sampling efficiency of Large Language Models for already existing reasoning patterns. This optimization often narrows the models' overall reasoning capacity at higher pass@k values, contrasting with distillation, which effectively expands their problem-solving scope.

likes.title: Reasoning Models Can Be Effective Without Thinking
likes.summary: Ma et al. demonstrated that Large Language Models trained for Chain-of-Thought reasoning can achieve comparable or superior performance without generating explicit reasoning steps, utilizing a technique called 'NoThinking'. This approach significantly reduces inference latency by up to 9x and token usage by up to 5.1x, particularly when combined with parallel sampling, offering a more efficient paradigm for LLM reasoning.

likes.title: Synthetic Data Generation & Multi-Step RL for Reasoning & Tool Use
likes.summary: SWiRL is an offline multi-step reinforcement learning methodology designed to enhance Large Language Models' reasoning and tool-use capabilities. It generates and utilizes synthetic data, applying process-based filtering for step-wise optimization, which leads to substantial performance gains and strong cross-domain generalization in complex tasks.

likes.title: ReTool: Reinforcement Learning for Strategic Tool Use in LLMs
likes.summary: ReTool, developed by ByteDance Seed, introduces a reinforcement learning framework that enables Large Language Models to strategically use code interpreters for complex problem-solving. It achieved 67.0% accuracy on the AIME 2024 benchmark, significantly improving performance over text-based reasoning and demonstrating emergent self-correction capabilities in code generation.

likes.title: Hogwild! Inference: Parallel LLM Generation via Concurrent Attention
likes.summary: Researchers from Yandex, HSE University, and IST Austria developed "Hogwild! Inference," a protocol enabling multiple Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate text concurrently by sharing a dynamically updated attention Key-Value (KV) cache. This mechanism allows LLMs to self-organize and collaborate in real-time, achieving up to 3.6x speedup and improved accuracy on complex reasoning tasks.

likes.title: Challenges and Paths Towards AI for Software Engineering
likes.summary: This paper presents a strategic roadmap for the field of AI in software engineering, providing a comprehensive taxonomy of software development tasks and identifying nine key bottlenecks that impede current AI capabilities. It proposes a targeted set of research directions focused on data collection, training, and inference-time approaches to advance automated software development.

likes.title: DAPO: An Open-Source LLM Reinforcement Learning System at Scale
likes.summary: Researchers from ByteDance Seed, Tsinghua University, and The University of Hong Kong developed DAPO, an open-source reinforcement learning system for large language models. The system achieved 50 points on the AIME 2024 dataset with a Qwen2.5-32B model, surpassing the prior 47-point score of DeepSeek-R1-Zero-Qwen-32B while requiring 50% fewer training steps.

likes.title: Proof or Bluff? Evaluating LLMs on 2025 USA Math Olympiad
likes.summary: Researchers from ETH Zurich and INSAIT conducted the first evaluation of large language models on generating rigorous natural language proofs for problems from the 2025 USA Mathematical Olympiad. The study found that most state-of-the-art models scored below 5% of the maximum points, with the highest-performing model, GEMINI-2.5-PRO, achieving only 24.4%, demonstrating fundamental shortcomings in advanced mathematical reasoning capabilities.

likes.title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
likes.summary: DeepSeek-AI developed DeepSeek-R1, an LLM demonstrating that sophisticated reasoning capabilities can emerge through pure outcome-based reinforcement learning without reliance on human-annotated reasoning trajectories. The model achieved an AIME 2024 pass@1 accuracy of 77.9% with R1-Zero, and the multi-stage DeepSeek-R1 surpassed state-of-the-art models on numerous math, coding, and STEM benchmarks while exhibiting emergent self-reflection and dynamic strategy adaptation.

likes.title: ReSearch: Learning to Reason with Search for LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
likes.summary: The ReSearch framework enables Large Language Models to integrate multi-step reasoning with external search, learning interactively via reinforcement learning without supervised intermediate steps. It yields substantial performance gains on complex multi-hop question answering benchmarks and reveals emergent self-correction capabilities.

likes.title: Insights into DeepSeek-V3: Scaling Challenges and Reflections on Hardware for AI Architectures
likes.summary: DeepSeek-V3 showcases how a hardware-software co-design strategy can achieve state-of-the-art large language model performance using a comparatively modest cluster of 2,048 NVIDIA H800 GPUs. The paper highlights innovations like Multi-head Latent Attention, DeepSeekMoE, FP8 mixed-precision training, and a Multi-Plane Fat-Tree network, which collectively reduce memory consumption, lower training costs, and accelerate inference.

likes.title: One-Minute Video Generation with Test-Time Training
likes.summary: Researchers from NVIDIA and leading universities introduce Test-Time Training (TTT) layers within pre-trained Diffusion Transformers to generate one-minute-long videos from text storyboards, enabling coherent multi-scene narratives while addressing the computational limitations of traditional self-attention mechanisms for long sequences.

likes.title: Sequential Task Assignment and Resource Allocation in V2X-Enabled Mobile  Edge Computing
likes.summary: A multi-tier task offloading mechanism for V2X-enabled Mobile Edge Computing efficiently processes sequential subtasks from vehicular applications by first leveraging proximate vehicle resources and then RSU-based MEC. The system minimizes energy consumption while meeting stringent delay requirements through joint optimization of offloading decisions, communication, and computation resource allocation, demonstrating superior performance over various baselines.

likes.title: How new data permeates LLM knowledge and how to dilute it
likes.summary: Research from Google DeepMind reveals how new knowledge permeates through large language models, demonstrating that surprising information (measured by token probability) leads to broader changes across model behavior, while introducing "stepping-stone" text augmentation and "ignore-k" update pruning techniques that reduce undesirable priming effects by 50-95%.

likes.title: Titans: Learning to Memorize at Test Time
likes.summary: Titans introduces a new neural memory module that learns to memorize information at test time and effectively combines with attention mechanisms for better long-term sequence modeling

likes.title: PHYBench: Holistic Evaluation of Physical Perception and Reasoning in  Large Language Models
likes.summary: PHYBench, a new benchmark developed by the School of Physics at Peking University, rigorously evaluates large language models' physical perception and reasoning using 500 original, human-curated physics problems. Evaluations revealed a substantial performance gap between LLMs and human experts, with the best LLM achieving 36.9% accuracy compared to the human baseline of 61.9%.

likes.title: Transformers without Normalization
likes.summary: This research introduces Dynamic Tanh (DyT), a simple element-wise function designed as a drop-in replacement for normalization layers in Transformers. Models equipped with DyT achieve performance comparable to or exceeding their normalized counterparts across a wide range of tasks including computer vision, large language models, and speech processing, often without requiring extensive hyperparameter tuning.
